questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The October 19, 1987 stock crash and its causes and responses
The Louvre Accord negotiations and the dollar's decline in 1987
The history of portfolio insurance and index futures trading
New Zealand's economic recovery after the crash of 1987
questions.explain: It covers the crash, its possible causes, liquidity problems and the Fed response.

questions.q: By what percent did the DJIA fall on Black Monday?
options: 12 percent
18 percent
22.6 percent
3.8 percent
questions.explain: The DJIA fell 508 points, or 22.6 percent.

questions.q: Why were large selling pressures expected on Monday even though markets were closed over the weekend?
options: Regulators required banks to sell large holdings before the Monday opening
Mutual fund customers could redeem shares at Friday prices, forcing fund sales
The Louvre Accord expired on the weekend, unsettling currency traders
Margin loans were automatically cancelled over the weekend by clearinghouses
questions.explain: Redemption requests far exceeded cash reserves, forcing large sales when markets opened.

questions.q: What did Greenspan's statement on October 20 do?
options: Ended the slide permanently by cutting interest rates a full point
Announced a halt in trading at the New York exchange until Friday
Sparked a rally of about 2,000 points that held through the week
Briefly lifted markets about 200 points before gains were erased
questions.explain: The market rallied about 200 points, but by noon gains were erased.

questions.q: What difference in central bank behavior explains New Zealand's worse outcome?
options: It refused to loosen monetary policy
It raised margin requirements
It provided too much liquidity
It closed its stock exchange
questions.explain: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand refused to loosen policy, with sharply negative, longer-term consequences.
